title: Safe Deploys: Canary, Blue-Green & Rollback for Data Pipelines

scenes.heading: Safe Deploys
scenes.subheading: Ship pipeline changes without breaking data
scenes.narration: Safe deploy strategies let you ship pipeline changes with confidence, limiting blast radius and giving you a fast way back if something goes wrong.

scenes.heading: Canary vs blue-green
scenes.narration: A canary deploy sends a small slice of work through the new version first, watches the metrics, and only then ramps up, which naturally limits the blast radius. Blue-green instead runs two complete environments and switches all traffic at once, giving you an instant rollback simply by switching back. Canary favors gradual confidence; blue-green favors clean, atomic cutovers.

scenes.heading: What makes deploys safe for data
bullets: Idempotent jobs so a rollback rerun is clean
scenes.narration: Idempotent jobs mean that rerunning after a rollback produces clean data rather than duplicates. Backward-compatible schema changes let old and new versions coexist during the transition. Validation gates verify the new output before it is promoted to consumers, and a tested one-command rollback ensures recovery is fast when you need it most.

scenes.heading: A canary deploy flow
scenes.narration: You deploy the new version alongside the old and route a small share of partitions through it. You then validate the output and the reliability metrics against the baseline. If everything looks healthy you ramp to full traffic, and if the checks fail you roll back immediately before most data is affected.

scenes.text: Never deploy without a rollback plan. Validate output on a small slice first, and make reverting as fast as shipping.
scenes.narration: Never deploy a pipeline change without a rollback plan, validate the output on a small slice first, and make reverting just as fast and routine as shipping.
